_readme: Creative Style questions and the six styles (BRIEF 8.4). The styles come from the book's chapters; the question wording and summaries are ours. Self-report, for fun, not a validated assessment.

styles.name: Scavenger
styles.summary: You notice what other people walk past. For you, ideas are already lying around: in a frustrating queue, an odd workaround, someone else's shop window.

styles.name: Connector
styles.summary: You smash unconnected things together and see what falls out. A comparison from a different world is often how you crack a problem.

styles.name: Shoe Swapper
styles.summary: You think about the person on the other end first. Looking through someone else's eyes is how you find what a problem is really about.

styles.name: Far-Out Dreamer
styles.summary: You think big and tell the story that makes people want to come along. Your risk is staying in the clouds; your gift is making a bold idea feel possible.

styles.name: Idea Chef
styles.summary: You throw a lot of ideas at the wall and let quantity do the work. Fast, playful and a little messy, which is exactly how a good spaghetti session should feel.

styles.name: Ruthless Editor
styles.summary: You can tell quickly which ideas deserve your time and money, and you are not shy about cutting the rest. Pair yourself with someone who makes plenty of raw material.

questions.prompt: When I get stuck on a problem, I usually…

options.text: go out and look at how the problem shows up in everyday life.
ask what two unrelated things I could mash together.
imagine how someone completely different would handle it.

questions.prompt: At the start of a project, my first move is to…

options.text: decide what the real goal is and what I am going to ignore.
picture the biggest, boldest version of the finished thing.
write down as many ideas as I can, good or bad.

questions.prompt: In a team meeting, I am the one who…

options.text: asks how the person on the other end will feel.
keeps ideas coming and says no idea is a bad idea.
brings in an example I spotted somewhere else.

questions.prompt: The best part of a creative session is…

options.text: when the idea gets big enough to excite people.
when we finally cut the list down to the few that matter.
when two odd ideas suddenly fit together.

questions.prompt: People who know me would say I…

options.text: can tell quickly which ideas will not work.
always have a note, a photo or a clipping of something interesting.
find links between things other people never connect.

questions.prompt: When someone brings me a new idea, I…

options.text: add three more ideas on top of it.
try to see it from the point of view of the people it is for.
ask how far it could go if there were no limits.
daydreaming about something I would love to build one day.
sorting out a messy plan until it makes sense.
wandering somewhere new and seeing what I notice.

questions.prompt: When I explain an idea, I tend to…

options.text: start with who it helps and why they would care.
show a pile of options and let people react.
compare it to something from a completely different world.

questions.prompt: If a project is going badly, I…

options.text: look for a surprising idea from another field.
generate a fresh batch of ideas right away.
go back out and look for what I have been missing.

questions.prompt: When it is time to choose between ideas, I…

options.text: score them against the goal and drop the weakest.
choose the one that would matter most to the people using it.
choose the one that makes me want to tell the story.
